headline: Nvidia board opens probe into CEO Huang over alleged Chinese spy link as crypto hits two-month lows
subhead: Bitcoin touched 73,708 dollars and ether 2,223, lowest since August, while the Nifty slipped 0.2 percent to 24,986.4 in Muhurat trading ahead of Tuesday's US CPI.

us.text: The S&P 500 rose 0.3 percent to 7,376.9 and the Nasdaq 1.1 percent on Friday as chipmakers recovered part of Thursday's rout; the Dow fell 0.5 percent.
Nvidia's board opened an independent probe into CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a woman US intelligence reportedly says is a Chinese spy; Huang stays on as CEO.
Hot October payrolls pushed implied odds of a December Fed hike back above 75 percent ahead of Tuesday's October CPI report.

india.text: Nifty slipped 0.2 percent to 24,986.4 and Sensex closed at 80,999.4 in Sunday's Muhurat session as early gains faded on profit taking.
Foreign investors were roughly flat and domestic institutions sold a net 700 crore rupees in the Muhurat session, provisional data show.
The rupee ended last week at 93.89 per dollar; a credible US-Iran deal could lift it toward 92, Business Standard reports.

global.text: The Nikkei rose 1.6 percent in early Monday trade after its steepest weekly fall since March, while the Kospi was little changed.
Europe fell on Friday, with the DAX down 1.9 percent and the FTSE 100 down 1.0 percent on the US tech rout and hot payrolls.
Bitcoin fell to 73,708 dollars and ether to 2,223, their lowest since August, on fears a Democratic Congress toughens crypto rules.

calendar.what: China October CPI and PPI; Constellation Energy, Occidental Petroleum, KKR, Take-Two and Skydance results; Fed's Bowman and Goolsbee speak
US October CPI; NSE and BSE closed for Diwali Balipratipada; China's rare earth export pause expires; CoreWeave results
US Veterans Day, bond market closed; OPEC monthly oil market report
India October CPI; US jobless claims and existing home sales; UK third quarter GDP; Cisco and Applied Materials results; Rezera US IPO expected
Anthropic IPO roadshow reported to start, price range not yet set; vVardis US IPO expected; about ten Fed officials speak during the week

weekly.narrative: The US midterms set the tone: a relief rally on Wednesday gave way to Thursday's AI chip rout on fears a Democratic Congress curbs data center building, and Friday's partial rebound and a 165,000 payrolls beat still left the S&P 500 down 2.7 percent and the Nasdaq 3.4 percent on the week. India went the other way, with foreign buying and cheaper crude lifting the Nifty 8.6 percent on the week and above 25,000 on Friday, while Kospi and the Nikkei bore the brunt of the chip selloff. Hopes of an Iran deal drove WTI down 12.8 percent on the week, and gold rose 4.5 percent and silver 5.5 percent despite rising Fed hike bets, while Bitcoin slipped 3.4 percent. Next week brings US CPI on 10 November, India CPI on 12 November, China's rare earth export pause expiring and a reported start to Anthropic's IPO roadshow.
